desc: Construct a graph with $2N$ nodes where node $i$ represents being at vertex $i$ in the original orientation and node $i+N$ represents being at vertex $i$ in the reversed orientation.
Add directed edges with weight 1: for each original edge $u \to v$, add an edge $u \to v$ (weight 1) and an edge $(u+N) \to (v+N)$ (weight 1).
Add bidirectional edges with weight $X$: for each vertex $i$ from 1 to $N$, add edges $i \to (i+N)$ and $(i+N) \to i$ with weight $X$.
Write the Python solution implementing Dijkstra's algorithm starting from node 1 to find the shortest distances to all nodes.
Output the minimum of the distance to node $N$ and node $N+N$ (which corresponds to reaching vertex $N$ in the reversed state).
